svg.title: (LCN1) proves the activity assertion in (LCN3). Thus the analytic recovery uses a signed estimate obtained by a finite interpolation cancellation, with the exact exponent 301, rather than assuming analyticity of arbitrarily selected primitive witnesses. In fact the output values are independent of such incidental choices. To compare two representatives with identical coupling and activity data, use the same constant affine input line but select the first representative at t = 0 and the second at t ̸= 0. The bounds (LCN3) still hold. For q ≥4, the signed measure δt −δ0 has moment price at most |t| at either radius. Therefore its two output differences are bounded by d|t| and fi|t|; letting t →0 proves equality. This supplies the single-valued activity and scalar maps on the common normed presentation.
